summary: This work demonstrates integration of Purcell filters into multilayer PCBs for superconducting quantum processors, with each embedded triangular patch antenna filter coupling to up to nine readout resonators and providing ~1000-fold radiative isolation at the qubit frequency. Experimental validation on a 35-qubit OQC-Toshiko device achieved median $T_1 = 84$ µs and $T_2^{\mathrm{echo}} = 110$ µs while maintaining fast readout with external quality factors $Q_{\mathrm{ext}} \sim 8 \times 10^3$.
motivation: Purcell filtering in superconducting qubits requires careful layout to balance readout speed against coherence; existing on-chip solutions increase substrate complexity and device footprint, motivating a scalable off-chip integration approach.
method: A 9–1 multiplexed filter was designed as a short-circuited triangular patch antenna at 9.8 GHz in a three-layer Rogers RT/duroid PCB with 0.9 GHz bandwidth, tiled to six filters (four 9–1 and two 3–1) for 35-qubit multiplexing, and validated via finite-element eigenmode simulations and cryogenic measurements at 11 mK.
result: All measured qubit $T_1$ values exceeded the 39 µs no-filter radiative limit (best $T_1 = 128$ µs), confirming Purcell protection; simulations predicted $\sim 28$ dB suppression of radiative decay at 4.4 GHz with resonator bandwidth spanning 700 MHz.
